title: A gift for my sons
author: titibiri
selftext:
Hello, everyone! 

 I have a game I play with my kids: they draw a character (usually a knight with glowing swords or monsters) and I ask Gemini to create a realistic version of their drawing. They love it!

So I had an idea for a Christmas present for them: to make a game featuring the characters they have drawn over time.

I thought about creating an arena where they are knights fighting off spawning monsters using their swords, axes, shields, etc. The younger one also loves magic, especially spells with big explosions.

I thought about having the monsters drop increasingly fancy and glowing armor and swords. The characters would evolve over time, fighting progressively harder monsters in different arenas.

I started creating the game using Claude, and it's helping me build it with "Three.js". However, the character models look really bad (blocky, like 1990s games). I want something closer to Zelda, The Witcher, and Dark Souls so they can actually recognize their drawings in the monsters and characters.

I have access to Claude (with a limited number of prompts) and Copilot Pro (both provided by the company I work for). What other AI do I need? I saw that Meshy AI creates 3D models. I thought about using it to generate the 3D characters, weapons, etc. Is it worth it?

My budget is tight (\~20 USD/month), and I can spend about 30 minutes to 1 hour per day working on this project.

I am not a programmer. Do you think this is possible? If so, what do you recommend I do?  
My kids mean everything to me. Thank you so much to anyone who can help.

comments.author: CaptainAlexWest
comments.body: I would download vscode or cursor then add claude or codex to it. Pick the system to play it on. Three.js does the browser it would play on everything. You have to meshly or blender the character out then add it to three.js. Ask chatgpt or claude chat to guide you how to build it out. Its design doc then prototype then meshes then final detail sweep. Everything connects to the ai with mcp servers. Codex does alot with 20 dollars. Three.js can do it but a real game engine would work out better. There is unity, godot and unreal. Ask the ai what path to take.

comments.author: Express-Room3441
comments.body:
In my opinion, this is the simplest path to what I think you are looking for. I dont want to say that a quality 3D game is totally out of reach for you, but definitely not happening in 3js and nearly impossible in 3 months 1hr/day with no experience. A 2D top down battle arena with enemies and loot would be very achievable though and could still look pretty great. 

1. Set up a coding harness. I use gpt and it was as simple as downloading codex and signing into my openai account. This lets the ai create code files for you.

2. Download Godot. Simplest game engine, especially for 2d, everyone is using it right now. Create an empty blank project and put your character images in project folder. 

3. Start a new chat in codex/Claudecode and select the Godot game folder as the workspace. Prompt something like, "Make x game from scratch in the empty Godot project with such and such game mechanics. Use image y and z in the asset folder as the playable character and enemy etc etc." The better your description the better the game will be. Seriously write a book. You may need to explicitly tell the ai to generate new sprites with transparent background using the existing images as a reference.

4. Play the game it makes for you and tell it to change what you dont like, add features, fix bugs, generate more assets, etc. Keep going until its done, then tell the ai to export the game as an exe.

Just like that you have a redistributable pc game. Godot and the coding harness work together to make it dead simple, the ai will create files and write all the code, then test your game until its working (may need to actually tell it the path to godot.exe for testing). If you arent currently paying for an AI that 20/month will get you gpt plus which can do this all no problem. Very little technical knowledge needed and if you get stuck you can always just ask the AI for help.

comments.author: EconomySerious
comments.body: i would browse steam and check games with that description

comments.author: Ok-File-2759
comments.body: Blender 5.1 is open source and free and has a great mcp. I connect codex to it and use it for my 3d assets. It’s not hyper realistic, but definitely not blocky, but this is a limitation of the AI model not blender so I’m hoping Astra will be better at making hyper realistic 3d assets. It might take a couple passes to get it how you want, but I’ve been using it every day and love it. Codex (and I assume Claude as well) can fully build, rig, and animate the characters for you with the mcp.

comments.author: ArS-13
comments.body:
You can try out tencent hunyuan global for creating 3d assets. You have daily tokens to spend for free and you can download the models for free. If you want to go the 3d route you have a few YouTube videos ahead of you especially creating a movable character can take a while especially if you need to fine tune some models.

Otherwise instead of creating 3d assets and a 3d arena game... You could look for an option to maybe 3d print those designs and paint them up? 

I don't know how old your kids are but my son (4) loves his models I printed for him with a Duplo tile as a base so I can play with them on his own.

So instead of a video game you could consider making a boardgame out of it and let the ai come up with the rules for combat and movement and such. 

Personally I'm thinking 3d without experience might be bit hard but as it's for your kids - it's a great project you should definitely try it out!

Oh and lastly what's about something like a 2d side view game? The artworks should be 2d already so maybe you could rather work on that?

replies.author: titibiri
replies.body: Thank you! I don’t have a 3d printer, but I’m considering a 2d game too
